key_insight: The title argues that as AI makes criticism easier to generate at scale, peer review needs a threshold for which critiques require a response. This summary is inferred from the title; the supplied abstract contains no substantive findings or methodological details.
problem_solved: AI-assisted criticism could overwhelm authors and reviewers if every generated objection creates an obligation to investigate or respond.
method: Conceptual focus inferred from the title: examine how scalable AI-assisted criticism changes peer-review workloads.
Central proposal indicated by the title: establish an obligation threshold for responding to criticism.
The supplied material does not specify threshold criteria, experiments, or validation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the issue is how to preserve rigorous scrutiny without letting inexpensive, high-volume criticism create disproportionate response burdens. A clearly defined threshold could help distinguish actionable critiques from those that do not warrant further work.

paper_title: When AI-assisted criticism scales, peer review needs an obligation threshold
